title: What Would Change the Decision?
scene: You have set a threshold before running a test. Now you ask a harder question: which information is actually worth collecting?
sceneJa: 追加分析を依頼する前に、その情報によって実際の意思決定が変わるかを問い、判断に関係する不確実性だけを減らす場面。

chunks.ja: さらにデータを集めることはできます
私たちの判断を変えるわけではありません
追加の分析を依頼する前に
私たちが何を違って行うのか

chunks.en: if the result came back high or low.
chunks.ja: 結果が高く出た場合と低く出た場合に

chunks.en: If our action would be the same either way,
chunks.ja: どちらの結果でも取る行動が同じなら

chunks.en: may not be worth the time.
chunks.ja: 時間をかける価値がないかもしれません
不確実性を減らします
その意思決定にとって

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: what we would do differently / if the result came back high or low
what we / would do differently if / the result came / back high or low
what we would / do differently if the result / came back / high or low
questions.explanation: The first version keeps ‘what we would do differently’ as one complete idea and the if-clause as its condition.

questions.question: What does ‘either way’ mean here?
options: Whichever of the two results we get
Using two methods at the same time
questions.explanation: ‘Either way’ means that the same statement applies whichever of two possibilities occurs.

questions.question: When might extra information NOT be worth collecting?
options: When it is difficult to visualize.
When the decision would be the same regardless of the result.
When the result might be surprising.
questions.explanation: If no possible result would change the action, collecting more information may add cost without improving the decision.

speak: Sound like you are challenging unnecessary analysis, not rejecting data itself. Stress ‘differently’ in ‘what would we do differently?’ and ‘matters’ in ‘uncertainty that actually matters to the decision’.
review: Previous session: ‘what would make us stop’, ‘in advance’, and ‘rather than defend it’. Today adds a value-of-information filter: before collecting more data, ask whether any plausible result would actually change the decision.
